basics.name: Francesco Cancelliere
basics.label: Robotics Research Engineer
basics.summary: Hands-on Robotics Engineer bridging physical mechatronics, embedded systems, and autonomous navigation. Skilled in taking complex robotic platforms from blank-canvas CAD design and machining to RTOS firmware, ROS 2 integration, and real-world field validation.

work.name: RobotiXX Lab - George Mason University
highlights: Co-developed CHUTNI (IROS 2026), an off-road holonomic robot: designed a rocker suspension with inter-axle differential, a 3-DoF active stabilization gimbal (±20° pitch/roll), and 1:2 gear turret in Autodesk Fusion 360.

Engineered Verti-Wheeler v2, a 1/10th scale rock crawler: fabricated chassis parts in-house (metal machining, 3D printing) and integrated 4WD differential locks, low/high gear servos, optical flow, and C++/micro-ROS firmware on Teensy.
Led real-world hardware deployments for Adaptive Dynamics Orchestration (ADO), a dynamic multi-model MPC framework achieving a 30% reduction in trajectory modeling error on complex off-road terrain.

Mentored the GMU team to 1st place overall at the 2026 Raytheon Autonomous Vehicle Competition, advising multi-robot hardware/software integration for GPS-denied VSLAM navigation and drone takeoff/landing on a moving UGV.

work.name: Deepsensing S.r.l.
highlights: Supervised edge vision deployment and model optimization on embedded hardware platforms (NVIDIA Jetson, Hailo-8 SDK, Intel ARRIA 10 FPGA).
Conducted hardware performance benchmarking to evaluate throughput, power efficiency, and real-time execution across edge AI accelerators.

work.name: Faradex S.r.l.
highlights: Translated client system requirements into technical specifications, rapid prototyping concepts, and hardware architecture for 5+ commercial embedded products.
Developed low-level firmware and RTOS (FreeRTOS) on resource-constrained microcontrollers (STM32, ESP32), handling component sourcing and low-power management.
Executed end-to-end product bring-up, electronic testing, hardware validation (oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, JTAG), and transition from prototype to full production.

work.name: Rosys Group - University of Catania
highlights: Owned full-stack mechatronics and software integration for an autonomous beach cleanup robot (SandRo), driving the platform from proof-of-concept prototype to live field deployment in 6 months.
Engineered high-level perception and manipulation (ROS, Python, YOLOv5, UR10e arm, MoveIt) and integrated low-level motor controllers for reliable outdoor operation on sand.

courses: Leading applied research on autonomous mobile platforms for navigation in unstructured environments, developing multi-modal LiDAR and RGB vision models and sim-to-real workflows.
Validated navigation policies through extensive field testing on physical off-road robot hardware.

Mentored and led a team of 3 MSc students for 2 consecutive years in NXP Cup autonomous racing competition, achieving 3rd and 1st best times overall with a custom vacuum-assisted downforce vehicle for maximum cornering grip.
Designed and built a motorized smart walker for mobility assistance, integrating actuators, embedded sensors, and an adaptive shared-control scheme for safe human-in-the-loop navigation.
